result.request: Fictional enterprise scenario: We want HireRight screening updates in our recruiting system within five minutes. For this scenario only, the customer says HireRight sandbox access is available. A technical owner can investigate a receiving HTTPS endpoint. The destination recruiting system API has not yet been reviewed. Explain what this new information changes and what remains unverified.

assessment.summary: The stated sandbox access and available technical owner enable a narrowly scoped, non-production prototype of HireRight push delivery to a customer-controlled HTTPS receiver. This changes the next step from validating whether a test can be attempted to testing actual receipt and acknowledgement behavior. It does not establish an end-to-end integration with the recruiting system, because that system’s API, authentication, update model, and operational ownership have not been reviewed. A five-minute visible-update commitment cannot yet be made.
assessment.endpoint: A customer-controlled HTTPS receiving endpoint that accepts HireRight status-update messages, records their arrival, and returns the required successful HTTP acknowledgement. The prototype should not assume that this endpoint can update the recruiting system until its API is reviewed.
assessment.expectedResult: Evidence that sandbox status changes reach the receiver, the receiver successfully acknowledges them, and delivery/recovery behavior can be observed. This proves only the HireRight-to-receiver segment; it does not prove that a status is displayed in the recruiting system within five minutes.

evidence.claim: HireRight documentation recommends push status updates to a client HTTPS endpoint; a successful HTTP acknowledgement represents receipt, and optional redelivery must be configured.
HireRight requests require HireRight-provided integration, company, user, subscription-key, and API-version headers; user identity affects available privileges.

unknowns: The customer-supplied sandbox access and its permissions/configuration are not independently verified.
Whether the HireRight sandbox can be configured to deliver push updates to the proposed receiver, including any redelivery configuration.
Whether the recruiting system exposes an API that can securely accept and visibly apply these updates, and who will operate failure handling and reconciliation.

No trustworthy source-event timestamp has been established. Therefore, end-to-end timing from HireRight’s actual status-change time to visible recruiting-system update cannot yet be measured. Receipt-to-receiver timing would measure only the downstream delivery segment.
Order or status completion must not be treated as hiring clearance without separate business and adjudication rules.
assessment.nextTest: The customer technical owner should provision a sandbox HTTPS receiver with request and acknowledgement logs, obtain/confirm the required sandbox credentials and permissions, configure a test push destination if available, and trigger known sandbox status changes. Expected evidence: captured deliveries, HTTP acknowledgement outcomes, any redelivery behavior, and arrival timestamps. The integration owner should then separately review the recruiting-system API and identify how a received status would become a visible record update.
questions: Does the recruiting system provide an authenticated API or supported integration mechanism to update the relevant screening-status field, and is a non-production environment available?
What event should count as the required five-minute start time: HireRight’s status-change time, or receipt at the customer receiver?
